mutations.because: With the shape rule disabled, an email address, a non-user actor value such as operator or cli:erase-user, or a real id wrapped in whitespace all pass the --user check and reach open() unchanged, so the test fails on expect(message).toBe(USAGE_ERASE) because the caught message is a database error or TypeError rather than the usage string.
command: erase CLI refuses a user id that is not shaped like a minted id before opening anything

mutations.because: A rule stricter than safeId() mints would refuse some real ids, so a person could not be erased by id and an incomplete erasure could not be finished. 200 minted ids always include at least one f, and with the alphabet narrowed to 0-9a-e the first such id fails the test.
command: erase CLI accepts every id that safeId mints
